paras.en: When it is needed to compare two or more series of data having different units of measurement e.g. to compare weights of students of first year statistics class in a college with the heights of students of first year statistics class of another college, then relative dispersion is used. In relative dispersion case data and measure of dispersion have different units of measurement. Relative dispersion is always expressed in terms of coefficient of dispersion, ratio, and percentage.
